assets.content:
Subject: Add live chat to your site
Preview text: Start by inserting the provided Customerly script into your site’s head section.

Turn your website into a support channel

Hi there,

Put Customerly live chat on your website so customers have a direct place to start a support conversation.

The documented first step is specific: insert the provided Customerly script into your website’s `<head>` section. This installs the live-chat widget on your site.

Customerly is an AI helpdesk where the widget supports Aura answering first, with human agents able to take over conversations with context when needed. Your team stays part of the conversation.

The live-chat documentation walks you through the installation path for adding the widget to your website.

Set up live chat → https://docs.customerly.io/en/live-chat

- Customerly

selected_brief.user_request: Write exactly one English activation email from the Customerly team. Reader: A SaaS support lead who just opened a Customerly workspace and can edit their website. Ask them to do one thing: Set up live chat on their site. Use a specific, documented first step and explain why it helps this reader. Keep the email under 150 words excluding subject, preview and signature. Avoid unsupported access, plan, timing and outcome claims. Use one CTA with an exact documented destination if available.

selected_brief.mechanism: The documented first step is to insert Customerly's provided script into the website's <head>; this installs the live-chat widget that supports Aura-first conversations and contextual human takeover.
selected_brief.belief_shift: Before: the new workspace is not yet connected to the website. After: the reader understands the exact first installation step and why the widget is useful to their support workflow.
must_not_say: Do not claim installation takes a particular amount of time or only one line of code; the one-line evidence applies to the mobile SDK, not the website widget.
Do not claim the reader has access under a particular plan or that any feature is free.
Do not promise a resolution rate, faster replies, reduced costs, increased conversions or any other customer outcome.
Do not imply Aura is trained, enabled or ready to answer immediately after the script is installed.
Do not introduce pricing, migration, mobile SDKs, WhatsApp, Messenger, surveys, help-center setup, API integrations or security claims.
Do not ask the reader to do anything besides set up live chat.
Do not use more than one CTA.

reader_verdicts.what_it_sells: Customerly offers a website live-chat widget that lets customers start support conversations, with Aura answering first and human agents taking over with context, so my team would handle website support conversations through Customerly.
reader_verdicts.relevance_feedback: The profile establishes that I am a SaaS support lead, have just opened a Customerly workspace, and can edit our website, so adding Customerly live chat is directly relevant and technically plausible. The email additionally assumes that we want website chat and are ready to insert a script; our current channel needs, approval process, website stack, and desired AI involvement remain unknown.

brief.promise: Installing the Customerly widget creates the website live-chat surface where Aura can answer first and people can take over with conversation context.
brief.orientation: Customerly gives a SaaS support team a website live-chat widget where Aura and human agents can handle customer conversations together.
brief.arc: One activation step: connect the new workspace to the reader's website, explain the operational value of that connection, and send them directly to the live-chat installation documentation.
brief.sequence_rationale: A single activation email should lead with the requested task rather than pricing, migration, broad automation metrics or a sales narrative. The documented script installation is specific and executable, while the widget's AI-first response and contextual human takeover provide the strongest supported reason for a support lead to complete it. No alternative proposition is included because another benefit or CTA would weaken the one-action contract. The single thing that would most change this campaign: Can this source be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

emails.selection_reason: Installing the website widget is the reader's requested activation task, and the documented Aura-to-human handoff explains why that task matters to a SaaS support lead.

value_case.reader_benefit: The website gains a live-chat support surface where Aura can serve as the first responder and human agents can take over with context when needed.
value_case.mechanism: After the provided Customerly script is inserted into the website's <head> section, the live-chat widget supplies the website interface; Customerly documents that this widget supports Aura answering first and humans taking over with context.
decision_conditions: The reader must be able to edit the website's <head> section.
The widget installation does not by itself establish that Aura's knowledge or other AI settings have been configured.

claim_conditions: Describe inserting the provided script into the website's <head> as the documented first installation step.
Present Aura-first handling and contextual human takeover as widget capabilities, not as proof that they are already configured in this workspace.
emails.user_request: Write exactly one English activation email from the Customerly team. Reader: A SaaS support lead who just opened a Customerly workspace and can edit their website. Ask them to do one thing: Set up live chat on their site. Use a specific, documented first step and explain why it helps this reader. Keep the email under 150 words excluding subject, preview and signature. Avoid unsupported access, plan, timing and outcome claims. Use one CTA with an exact documented destination if available.
emails.job: Get the reader to install the Customerly live-chat widget on their website.
emails.single_idea: Add the provided Customerly script to the website's <head> so the support team can establish the live-chat surface where Aura can answer first and people can take over with context.
emails.felt_need: Turn the new Customerly workspace into a support channel customers can reach from the website.
emails.mechanism: The documented first step is to insert Customerly's provided script into the website's <head>; this installs the live-chat widget that supports Aura-first conversations and contextual human takeover.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the new workspace is not yet connected to the website. After: the reader understands the exact first installation step and why the widget is useful to their support workflow.
must_not_say: Do not claim installation takes a particular amount of time or only one line of code; the one-line evidence applies to the mobile SDK, not the website widget.
Do not claim the reader has access under a particular plan or that any feature is free.
Do not promise a resolution rate, faster replies, reduced costs, increased conversions or any other customer outcome.
Do not imply Aura is trained, enabled or ready to answer immediately after the script is installed.
Do not introduce pricing, migration, mobile SDKs, WhatsApp, Messenger, surveys, help-center setup, API integrations or security claims.
Do not ask the reader to do anything besides set up live chat.
Do not use more than one CTA.
emails.objection: Installing the widget should not remove the support team's ability to step into customer conversations; Customerly documents that humans can take over with context.
emails.tone: Direct, welcoming and action-oriented, with one short explanation of the support value.
emails.next_step_decision: Follow the documented installation path and add the Customerly widget to the website.
emails.next_step_value: The live-chat documentation provides the setup destination for adding the Customerly widget; the getting-started checklist identifies inserting the provided script into the site's <head> as the first step.
emails.next_step_limit: Opening the documentation does not install the widget, configure Aura's knowledge or demonstrate support outcomes.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the immediate website activation task unmistakable; signal the concrete live-chat setup step without promising speed or results.

directions: Produce exactly one English activation email.
Keep the body under 150 words, excluding subject, preview and signature.
Ask for one action only: set up live chat on the website.
Use one CTA with the exact documentation destination.
use: The documented first step: insert the provided script into the website's <head> section.
The widget's supported Aura-first and contextual human-takeover capability.
avoid: Unsupported access, plan, timing and outcome claims.
Additional setup tasks or secondary CTAs.
context_only: The reader has just opened a workspace and can edit the website.

brief.voice_notes: Use Customerly's direct, result-oriented voice, but keep this activation email practical rather than turning it into a sales pitch. Refer to Aura by name only when explaining the widget's operational value.

reasons: No persisted market recommendation applies to this campaign.
